new_statements.relation_note: Catalog records initial stress (initial stress); Staley, the SIL field linguist with ~13 years on the language and the only source with words longer than two syllables and a stress-contrast pair, places default stress on the penult with antepenult exceptions. The two coincide on disyllables (the bulk of the McGregor/OPD examples) and diverge on words of three or more syllables (Staley: waikópou, not *wáikopou). Also a type difference: catalog = strictly fixed initial; Staley = penult default with lexical antepenult exceptions (fixed: penultimate syllable with a marked minority).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default stress on the penultimate syllable; a small set of lexical exceptions carry antepenultimate stress, giving a (near-)minimal pair waikópou 'man's name' vs wákopou 'wooden pestle'. No weight condition stated. The same wording, plus 'the normal stress pattern is penultimate, with antepenultimate the only option' and 'Two syllable words are always stressed on the penultimate syllable', appears in Staley 1996 (LLM 27: 149, 150 fn. 5, 156), which is held held by the project but not in the works list.
new_statements.exceptions: 'a few words' with antepenultimate stress (lexical); contrastive pair (4)

readall_conflicts: The two readable sources disagree. The SIL OPD sheet (2004, compiled from the CMML/McGregor material and the catalog's own deciding source McGregor 1982 [written 1961]) says 'The first syllable is usually stressed', i.e. initial; Staley's dissertation (1995, published 2007, §2.2 p. 8) says 'Stress is mostly predictable, occurring on the penultimate syllable', with a few antepenultimate exceptions and a contrastive pair waikópou / wákopou. The statements coincide on disyllables, which are almost all of the OPD/McGregor example words, and diverge only on trisyllables and longer, where Staley's pair shows non-initial default stress. Staley is the trained field linguist with the longer exposure (1982-1990s), and repeats the penult rule with counts in his 1996 reduplication paper (LLM 27: 149, 150, 156: 'the normal stress pattern is penultimate, with antepenultimate the only option'; all 2-syllable and most 3-syllable words trochaic feet built from the right). The OPD's initial-stress line is a one-sentence, hedged summary of the 1961 impressionistic statement. No source reports tone or length.
